Reviewed all 6 walk-in sore throat visits from today. Five had POSITIVE rapid strep antigen tests (pt-1003, pt-1017, pt-1021, pt-1023, pt-1030); pt-1026 was negative (viral pharyngitis) and received no antibiotic.

Orders placed (all 10-day courses for GAS pharyngitis):
- pt-1003 (Maria Lopez, DOB 1958-03-14): amoxicillin 500 mg BID. Only allergy is sulfonamides.
- pt-1017 (Maria Lopez, DOB 1991-07-02): amoxicillin 500 mg BID. No allergies; asthma stable. (Note: two distinct patients share this name - verified by DOB/MRN.)

- pt-1023 (Elizabeth Martin): clindamycin 300 mg TID. A scanned 2015 outside urgent care record documents anaphylaxis (throat tightness, wheezing, hives, epinephrine) to penicillin VK in 2011 - this was NOT on her allergy list. I added the penicillin allergy (high criticality) to her chart and avoided all beta-lactams, including cephalosporins. Clindamycin chosen over a macrolide given her sertraline (QT considerations).
- pt-1030 (Daniel King): amoxicillin 500 mg BID. No allergies or other medications.

No drug-drug interaction concerns identified with existing medication lists. Please note pt-1023's newly documented severe penicillin allergy for future prescribing.
